title: Capital Letters
subject: geography
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Eleven stops, most of them seats of government.
completionMessage: Every seat filled, every border crossed.

entries.clue: Tibetan home of the Potala Palace
entries.explanation: The palace complex overlooking the city was the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas.

entries.clue: Once Philadelphia, now Jordan's largest city
entries.explanation: Under Hellenistic and Roman rule the city bore the name Philadelphia.

entries.clue: Kenyan city with a national park at its edge

entries.explanation: It stands on the Gulf of Guinea coast.
It was Christiania, then Kristiania, before taking its older name back.

entries.clue: Japan's kitchen, as the nickname goes
entries.explanation: Long a merchant and food city, it is called tenka no daidokoro, the nation's kitchen.

factCards.text: Norway's capital was called Christiania, later spelled Kristiania, from 1624 until it resumed the name Oslo in 1925.
Nairobi National Park, opened in 1946, sits on the southern edge of Kenya's capital and was the country's first national park.
factCards.sourceTitle: Kenya Wildlife Service — Nairobi National Park

factCards.text: The Potala Palace in Lhasa stands at roughly 3,700 metres above sea level and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1994.
factCards.sourceTitle: UNESCO World Heritage List — Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace
